findings.title: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid CSS property
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` but this property does not exist in any version of Internet Explorer or Edge. The correct IE10 property is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line produces dead CSS and suggests a copy-paste error. It should be removed.

findings.title: `order` mixin uses wrong value for old flexbox ordinal-group properties
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` use 1-based indexing, while the modern `order` property is 0-based. Passing `order(3)` (as done in header.scss for `.panel`) outputs `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3` which actually means position 2 in the old spec. The mixin should output `$val + 1` for these two properties to achieve equivalent ordering in older browsers.

findings.title: `float: right` on button is ignored inside flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (via `@include flexbox()`), but the `button` child still uses `float: right` to position itself at the trailing edge. Float has no effect on flex items, so the button will no longer be pushed to the right. It should use `margin-left: auto` or an `order` value instead.

findings.title: Removal of `.title` float rule may break layout if `.title` elements exist outside flex context
findings.body: The diff removes the `.d-header .title { float: left; }` rule entirely. If any markup still contains a `.title` element inside `.d-header` but outside `.contents` (the new flex container), or if a plugin/theme relies on this rule, the element will lose its float. Within the flex container float is ignored anyway, so if `.title` is always inside `.contents` this is safe, but the removal is silent with no migration note.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin does not map modern keywords to legacy equivalents
findings.body: The mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. If a future caller passes `flex-start` or `flex-end` (valid modern values), the legacy properties will receive invalid values since they expect `start`/`end`. Currently only `center` and `baseline` are used (which are identical across specs), but the mixin's interface is misleading and will silently break with other valid inputs.
